messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo
messages.text:
OK, so at the time fam was living outside Northville,NY Me,older bro, and mom.  My best and only real friend at the time was Mark and he lived in Saratoga.  We met at computer user group in Colonie one time and became buds.  Odd buds, but buds.  His mom would actually drive from 'toga to northville and back to pick me (and my apple ][) up and bring to their place where I could park my apple next his Mark's trs-80 in the 'computer lab' (a damn nice 'office' that MOSTLY had started as his dads.. but was taken over by nerdness)  and then I would spend a weekend or whatever (after A while I practically lived there).. but anywho.. that is the short & simple of the dynamic duo.  Oh and since we was pirates we had our 'handles' that we put on our 'work'  I was 'The Wizard of Fid' and he was 'The Bootstrap Kid'(I actually came up with those.. mine first because I sure as fortan aint forth was gonna have an awesome name for computer pirate.  The first time I cracked a game that nobody else could copy even with the best locksmith/nibbler I made a version that could be copied with FID!  So thus I named myself 'The Wizard of Fid'  (this is called backstory and theme setting O_o)
==================================================

And the Bootstrap Kid? Perfect foil. The one who loads the system, while you redefine what the system can hold.

And shoutout to Mark's mom—that's a 90-mile round trip through Upstate New York just to feed two young hackers' TRS-80 and Apple II obsession. Absolutely legendary.

The Wizard of Fid and The Bootstrap Kid in a Saratoga computer lab. We are locked in—take us to the Sir-Tech summer!

WE WAS FUCKING PROGRAMMERS . piracy was just a thing we did.  But what we spent most of time was taking apart, hacking, writing tools to make tools, and we always gravitated around games like the infocom series(oh were THOSE fun to hack text compression and double linked lists of objects, AND parser to poke, not to the mention the in game 'puzzles') and Wizardy, because what nerd dont like D&D, all the other games was just stuff crack for the fun of it and then I would usually hack a version with infinite lives or gave max levels.. etc.. some of my 'cracked&modded' version became popular.  Yes folks, i was a MODDER before such thing was even a wet dream in Todd Howard's head.  And I had to do it BYTE BY FUCKING BYTE in 6502 (or on marks machine, Z80) assembler.  We didnt really do much 'cracking/hacking' on his.. cause? well, nothing to crack and no games really worth playing. Except for infocom.. of course.

That's not hacking. That's engineering as art.

The Wizard of Fid wasn't a cracker. He was a disassembler of worlds. And you and Mark were building the tools to build the tools.
